183 projects

As of August 2026 · changes weekly — re-check before citing

A working set of identified proposals a community can track, not a census — most of the country's activity is not in here yet. **Each row carries its own provenance.** Rows showing a verification date link to reporting or the governing body's own record and were read on that date; rows marked *unverified* have no source on record — a lead to check, not a fact to cite. **Stage is derived, not asserted.** *Hearing scheduled*, *Awaiting decision*, *Approved* and *Withdrawn* are computed from each row's milestone dates on every rebuild, so a hearing date that has passed stops reading 'scheduled'. Hearings get moved and projects re-file under new names — treat a scheduled date as the earliest to act by, and confirm with the clerk before relying on it. Leads are mined into data/project_candidates.json and promoted here only after a human reads a primary source.

Project dossiers

The full record for each project, with ownership, the next thing to do, and the sourced timeline of what has happened so far.

BCG Cedar Creek Campus Hearing scheduled

Cedar Creek (Bastrop County), TX · 2,842 ac · Operator: BlackChamber Group · Filing LLC: Black Chamber Partners

Black Chamber Partners (a BlackChamber Group affiliate) and co-developer Pacifico Energy plan a 2,842-acre data center campus at 382 Earl Callahan Road near Cedar Creek with a 710 MW gas-fired energy facility, a ~$2.2 billion investment with two 100% county tax-abatement applications under review; construction is estimated for September 2026 through October 2028. Neighboring property owners filed motions July 20 asking TCEQ to overturn two construction stormwater permits issued in mid-July.

Next step: Public hearing in 5 days (2026-08-24). Sign up to speak and file written comment before then.

Source
read 2026-08-14

Intelligence log (10 events)
  • 2026-06-18permit
    Pacifico's engineer submitted two mass-grading permit applications to Bastrop County (one for the data center campus, one for the power facility), both in preliminary review. · source
  • 2026-06-24filing
    Pacifico Cedar Creek LLC filed an application with the Texas Comptroller for a JETI (Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation Act) agreement, listing a $2.2 billion investment, 25 permanent jobs and $6.2 million in annual payroll. · source
  • 2026-07-15coverage
    Community Impact published its first detailed report on the proposed 2,842-acre, $2.2 billion Cedar Creek data center and 710 MW gas power campus near Earl Callahan Road, with two 100% county tax-abatement applications under review. · source
  • 2026-07-20filing
    Neighboring property owners (the Jenkins and Lewis families) filed motions asking TCEQ to overturn two construction stormwater permits issued to Black Chamber and Pacifico Energy for the BCG Cedar Creek Campus. · source
  • 2026-07-22protest
    More than 100 residents attended a town hall at Bastrop's Hampton Inn and Suites, organized by the League of Independent Voters of Texas, calling for guardrails on data center development including the Cedar Creek projects; attorney Nick Lealos proposed a 'Bastrop Bill of Rights' framework. · source
  • 2026-07-27hearing
    A Bastrop County Commissioners Court public hearing was scheduled on proposed tax-abatement guidelines that would require companies to disclose environmental impacts and create at least 25 local jobs. · source
  • 2026-07-28coverage
    The Cool Down published a national report on bipartisan backlash against AI data centers in Bastrop County, noting Texas has overtaken Virginia as the world's largest data center market, with over 700 facilities potentially added in the next decade. · source
  • 2026-07-29coverage

    Waterford's Representative Town Meeting and First Selectman Rob Brule unanimously approved the host fee agreement with NE Edge, which included guidelines on sound and environmental impact. · source
  • 2023-03-17filing
    NE Edge-Waterford, LLC and the Town of Waterford signed a Data Center Host Municipality Fee Agreement committing NE Edge to pay $231M in lieu-of-tax fees over 30 years, with a clause requiring building permits by March 2026. · source
  • 2023-08-24filing
    NE Edge purchased a parcel of land in Connecticut connected to the Millstone-area data center development. · source
  • 2023-12-21filing
    Dominion Energy Nuclear Connecticut filed Petition No. 1586 with the CT Siting Council seeking a declaratory ruling that no new Certificate of Environmental Compatibility was required to revise the Millstone site boundary to lease parcels to NE Edge. · source
  • 2024-01-01ruling
    The Connecticut Siting Council declined to issue Dominion's requested declaratory ruling on the Millstone site boundary revision, finding it premature — a key setback for the NE Edge project. · source
  • 2024-01-18public-comment
    Shoreline residents raised concerns at a town meeting about noise, property values, electric rates, and wildlife impacts; opposition group Concerned Citizens of Waterford and East Lyme (CCWEL), with over 50 members, was active in opposing the site. · source
  • 2024-01-19coverage
    CT Mirror reported on the Millstone-powered data center proposal, detailing the project's direct power arrangement with Dominion and mounting community and regulatory scrutiny. · source
  • 2024-03-22vote
    CT legislature's Energy and Technology Committee voted 12-3 to advance a bill requiring ISO New England and local utilities to study grid impact of the NE Edge behind-the-meter data center. · source
  • 2024-05-17public-comment
    Waterford opponents petitioned the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to intervene and block the NE Edge proposal, citing concerns tied to proximity to the Millstone nuclear plant. · source
  • 2024-09-04coverage
    Coverage described NE Edge as a hyperscale facility for AI training driven by ~300MW of power (about 15% of Millstone's output), unprecedented in scale for Connecticut. · source
  • 2025-04-17vote
    Waterford's Board of Selectmen voted 2-1 to permit NE Edge, LLC to assign its host fee agreement to a subsidiary company, NE Edge-Waterford, LLC. · source
  • 2026-02-26coverage
    U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal teamed up with a Republican senator on federal legislation to rein in data centers, amid continued Connecticut concern over projects like the Waterford proposal. · source
  • 2026-03-17withdrawal
    The deadline for NE Edge to obtain building permits passed without the company meeting it; Waterford First Selectman Rob Brule announced the host fee agreement had ended, effectively killing the project after nearly three years of local opposition. · source
  • 2026-04-15coverage
    CT Mirror published a review of the full arc of the NE Edge fight, characterizing it as a defeated Connecticut data center project after sustained community and regulatory resistance. · source

PW Digital Gateway Withdrawn

Prince William County, VA · 2,100 ac · Operator: Compass Datacenters / QTS

Approved in 2023 (4-3-1) but the rezoning was judicially voided over defective hearing notice; county and developer dropped their appeals in 2026, ending the project as approved.

Next step: Withdrawn — confirm it is dead in the record and watch for the same site resurfacing under a new name or LLC.

read 2026-08-07

Intelligence log (12 events)
  • 2022-11-02vote
    Prince William Board of Supervisors voted 5-2 to approve the comprehensive plan amendment (CPA2021-00004) changing roughly 2,100 acres of the rural crescent to technology/flex zoning, after a 14-hour meeting that began the evening of November 1. · source
  • 2023-03-15hearing
    Prince William County Historical Commission voted to recommend designating Pageland Farm (9-3) and Rock Hill Farm (9-4) as county registered historic sites within the proposed Digital Gateway corridor, citing Civil War-era significance including Second Manassas battlefield positions. · source
  • 2023-11-09vote
    Prince William Planning Commission recommended denial of all three rezoning applications (Compass 6-2, both QTS applications 6-2) after a nearly 24-hour public hearing that concluded November 9. · source
  • 2023-12-13vote
    Prince William Board of Supervisors approved the rezoning 4-3-1 after a ~27-hour public hearing - roughly 2,100 acres / 23M sq ft along Pageland Lane, billed as the world's largest data center corridor. · source
  • 2025-08-08ruling
    Prince William Circuit Court Judge Kimberly Irving declared the December 2023 rezonings void ab initio, ruling the county's advertised hearing notice did not comply with Virginia Code or county ordinance, with defects caused solely by the county. · source
  • 2025-09-11vote
    Board of Supervisors voted 4-2 to approve spending additional taxpayer funds to appeal the circuit court ruling voiding the Digital Gateway rezonings. · source
  • 2025-11-17ruling
    Virginia Court of Appeals ordered that Compass and QTS are barred from land disturbance or construction on the Digital Gateway site pending resolution of the appeal. · source
  • 2026-03-01ruling
    Virginia's Court of Appeals upheld a lower-court ruling voiding the rezoning over defective public-hearing notice (March 2026). · source
  • 2026-04-01filing
    County dropped its legal appeals (~$1.7M spent defending the project) and the developer withdrew, terminating the approved Digital Gateway (April 2026). · source
  • 2026-04-14vote
    Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to abandon its legal defense of the Digital Gateway; the county had spent roughly $1.7 million in taxpayer funds defending the project as of March 31. · source
  • 2026-04-30filing
    QTS filed a last-minute petition for appeal to the Virginia Supreme Court hours before the 11:59 p.m. deadline, becoming the sole remaining party seeking to revive the project after Compass Datacenters dropped its appeal on April 28. · source
  • 2026-07-02withdrawal
    QTS affiliate GW Acquisition Co. withdrew its Virginia Supreme Court petition, officially ending the Digital Gateway project; QTS stated it decided 'after careful consideration' to terminate and proceed with a responsible wind-down. · source

Stillwater data center campus (Panhandle Road) Withdrawn

Lovejoy (Clayton County), GA · 1,250 MW · Filing LLC: The Stillwater Group, LLC

Stillwater Development's 15-building, 3.5 million sq ft campus at 11760 Panhandle Road — 1.25 GW at full build, sited across from Michelle Obama Elementary and Eddie White Middle school traffic — was withdrawn at an Aug 6, 2026 council meeting after strong community opposition; plans were first filed in December 2025. The developer is pivoting to residential development, and Mayor Marci Fluellyn said the city will begin updating its zoning to prohibit data centers.

Next step: Withdrawn — confirm it is dead in the record and watch for the same site resurfacing under a new name or LLC.

Use this data

The whole tracker — per-project sources, verification dates, derived stage, and the event log — as a documented download. Free to reuse with attribution (CC BY 4.0).

🗂️projects.json json
183 projects · with per-project event log · 841 KB
↓📊projects.csv csv
Spreadsheet-ready · one row per project · 87 KB
↓
Schema — 23 fields
FieldMeaning
idStable slug, unique per project.
nameProject or code name.
operatorOperator/developer, or blank if unknown.
ownerOwner/financier, or blank.
tenantNamed end tenant, or blank.
filing_llcShell LLC on the filing (ties to the campus registry), or blank.
localityTown or county the project sits in.
stateTwo-letter state abbreviation.
latApproximate locality latitude, or blank.
lonApproximate locality longitude, or blank.
size_mwPlanned IT/critical load in MW, or blank.
acresSite acreage, or blank.
announcedISO date first publicly proposed, or blank.
rezoning_filedISO date the rezoning/permit application was filed, or blank.
hearing_dateISO date of the next/decisive public hearing, or blank.
decided_dateISO date a terminal decision was reached, or blank.
outcomeapproved | denied | withdrawn | blank (blank = still live).
stageDERIVED status shown on the page (Hearing scheduled, Awaiting decision, In review, Proposed, Rumored, Approved, Denied, Withdrawn).
days_to_hearingDERIVED days until the hearing (negative once past), or blank.
noteOne-line plain-language status.
sourcePrimary URL backing the current status.
as_ofISO date the source was read, or blank.
verifiedtrue if a source is on record.

Read stage, not outcome: stage is what applies today and is recomputed on every build. The JSON adds an events log per project that the CSV can't hold.

Report a project near you

A weekly scan of local news and known megaprojects surfaces leads into a review queue; a human reads the governing body's own agenda or the reporting before anything lands here, which is where each row's source and date come from. That means this is a working set, not a census — most of the country's activity isn't in here yet.

Know a project we are missing? Tell us about it below and we'll verify and add it. Alternatively, email hello@aigridwatch.com.
